rounds.text: Variman Global Enterprises Ltd is trading at a significant discount across multiple valuation metrics compared to sector benchmarks, with a P/E of 22.24x versus a sector benchmark of 33.03x and an EV/EBITDA of 11.61x against 22.37x [E6, E11]. This undervaluation is starkly disconnected from the company's robust operational expansion, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 41% and a massive 856% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E21]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at Rs 6 per share, providing a 31.0% margin of safety over the current market price of Rs 4.32, while reverse DCF expectations require a modest 12.9% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E43, E45]. Fundamental momentum is further reinforced by expanding operating margins—which rose to 6% in March 2026 from 2% three years prior—and improving working capital requirements dropping from 140 days to 96.4 days [E29, E59]. Conceded: the stock is currently lagging the market with an RS rating of 0, trading below its 200-day moving average, and exhibiting negative operating and free cash flows in March 2026 [E34, E35, E48, E49].

Conceded: the company trades at a lower P/E of 22.24x against a sector benchmark of 33.03x [E6], and an EV/EBITDA of 11.61x versus 22.37x [E11]. However, this multiple is applied to a business that generates severely compromised cash flows, reporting negative operating cash flow of Rs -3 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -6 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35]. While the bull highlights 856% trailing profit growth [E21], cash conversion stands at a dismal -1.00x, meaning reported profits completely fail to translate into actual cash entering the business [E33]. The bull's reliance on a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 6 [E43] is undermined by a history of poor capital returns, featuring a median ROE of just 3% over 10 years and 4% over 3 years [E25, E27]. Furthermore, while margins rose to 6% in March 2026 [E29], the yearly operating-margin trend remains explicitly inconsistent [E31], and borrowings have simultaneously expanded from Rs 15 Cr to Rs 23 Cr [E38]. Finally, the claim of fundamental momentum is heavily offset by a relative-strength rating of 0, a 30% three-year share price decline, and a severe 71% drop over the past twelve months [E23, E49, E50].
